overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by voting to adjourn its March 10 meeting and then reconvening to continue deliberating on a special permit, denying public access. It ordered future compliance and declined the other allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated outside a properly posted meeting by voting to adjourn its March 10 meeting and then reconvening to continue discussing a special permit.
allegations.key_passage: the fact remains that at least one member of the public who clearly had an interest in the topic being discussed left the meeting room after the Board voted to adjourn the meeting and the Board thereafter resumed deliberations about that particular matter.

allegations.summary: The minutes provided did not accurately reflect the Board's vote to adjourn after closing the public hearing, or the discussion about that vote.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the minutes do not accurately reflect the Board's vote to adjourn the meeting after it had voted to close the public hearing for case 20-15, or any discussion that took place with respect to the vote to adjourn.

allegations.summary: Complaint named the Board's chair and Town Counsel; allegations against Town Counsel were addressed.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law applies only to public bodies and their members; therefore, we decline to review any allegations that Town Counsel violated the Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised several additional allegations that the AG said would not constitute Open Meeting Law violations even if true.
allegations.key_passage: The Complainant raises several additional allegations that, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
